chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Musa narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, Allah will forgive him his past and future sins. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him the reward of one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified 'Umrah. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Ashura, it is as if he has visited Allah above His Throne.

key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on the 15th of Sha'ban and Day of 'Arafah?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the unique cosmological significance of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine by linking specific ziyarah dates to profound spiritual merits, such as the Day of 'Arafah’s reward of a thousand accepted pilgrimages. This tradition reflects the Shia emphasis on the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt, where visiting the Imam is elevated to a direct encounter with the Divine Presence, reinforcing the concept of *tawassul* through the Prophet’s family.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Mūsā narrated to me from ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Nahīk, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, who said: Ja’far ibn Muḥammad (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Allāh will forgive the past and future sins of those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha’bān. Allāh will register the reward of one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified ‘Umrah for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the Day of ‘Arafah. Those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the Day of ‘Āshūrā, it is as if they have gone to the Ziyārah of Allāh on top of His Throne.
